subject: Information Theory
title: Fourier's Gift
description: A quick win: understand Fourier's Gift.

hook.text: Every sound you hear—a violin, a voice, a car horn—is just a sum of pure sine waves at different frequencies.

buildup.text: Fourier proved in 1807 that any periodic signal can be decomposed into a sum of simple sine waves.

discovery.text: The Fourier transform converts a signal from time domain to frequency domain, revealing its hidden structure.

twist.text: This is why your phone equalizer works. It adjusts individual frequency bands, thanks to Fourier decomposition.

climax.text: MP3, JPEG, MRI, and speech recognition all depend on Fourier analysis. It's the backbone of signal processing.

punchline.text: Any signal is just sine waves in disguise.

quiz.question: What does the Fourier transform reveal?
options: The frequency components that make up a signal
